portal-01-namespace-overview.png.t: Host name — the address of your namespace. Your connection string begins Endpoint=sb:// followed by this name.
Pricing tier — Standard or Premium. Basic has no topics; queues work on every tier.
Settings → Shared access policies — where you create and copy the connection string ServiceHub uses.
Entities — your Queues and Topics live here.

portal-02-shared-access-policies.png.t: Add — creates a new policy. Make one just for ServiceHub, so you can revoke it without touching anything else.
RootManageSharedAccessKey — the namespace's default key, shared by everything. Do not hand this one to ServiceHub.
Any policy you already have for another tool — better not to share it. Give ServiceHub its own.

portal-03-add-policy.png.t: Policy name — for example servicehub-app, so you can recognise (and later revoke) it.
Manage — required. Azure lets only Manage list your queues and count their messages; without it ServiceHub cannot see them.
Send — used only when you press Replay, to put a copy of a dead letter back.
Listen — used to read queues and dead-letter queues.

portal-03b-add-policy-filled.png.t: Manage, Send and Listen. Azure ticks Send and Listen for you when you tick Manage — Manage includes them.
Create — saves the policy and generates its keys.

portal-04-policy-created.png.t: Your new policy appears in the list.

portal-05-connection-string.png.t: Claims — what this policy may do.
Primary connection string — click the eye to reveal, then the copy icon. Paste this into ServiceHub. Treat it like a password.
Copy to clipboard — copies the whole connection string.
Delete — the way to revoke ServiceHub's access later.

portal-06-queues.png.t: Queue name — ServiceHub finds every queue in the namespace; you do not list them.
Active messages — waiting to be processed.
Dead-letter messages — failed too often and were set aside. These are what ServiceHub shows on its Dead letters tab.

portal-07-queue-overview.png.t: Max delivery count — how many tries before Azure dead-letters a message. Here 3.
Message counts — Active and Dead-letter must match what ServiceHub shows.
Dead lettering on expiry is off — messages here are dead-lettered by delivery count or by your app, which is all ServiceHub needs.
